reference.title: Selecting updater sets for full Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) coverage
reference.shortdesc: You can select Clair updater sets to cover vulnerabilities in Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL). Use the rhel, rhcc, clair.cvss, and osv updater sets for full coverage.

section.p: For full coverage of vulnerabilities in Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), you must use the following updater sets:

ul.li: rhel. This updater ensures that you have the latest information on the vulnerabilities that affect RHEL.
rhcc. This updater keeps track of vulnerabilities related to Red Hat’s container images.
clair.cvss. This updater offers a comprehensive view of the severity and risk assessment of vulnerabilities by providing Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) scores.
osv. This updater focuses on tracking vulnerabilities in open-source software components. This updater is recommended due to how common the use of Java and Go are in RHEL products.

section.codeblock: #... updaters: sets: - rhel - rhcc - clair.cvss - osv #...

section.title: Advanced updater configuration
section.p: In some cases, users might want to configure updaters for specific behavior, for example, if you want to allowlist specific ecosystems for the Open Source Vulnerabilities (OSV) updaters.

Advanced updater configuration might be useful for proxy deployments or air-gapped deployments. Configuration for specific updaters in these scenarios can be passed by putting a key underneath the config environment variable of the updaters object. Users should examine their Clair logs to double-check names.
The following YAML snippets detail the various settings available to some Clair updaters.

note.p: For most users, advanced updater configuration is unnecessary.

section.title: Configuring the alpine updater
section.codeblock: #... updaters: sets: - alpine config: alpine: url: https://secdb.alpinelinux.org/ #...

section.title: Configuring the debian updater
section.codeblock: #... updaters: sets: - debian config: debian: mirror_url: https://deb.debian.org/ json_url: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/data/json #...

section.title: Configuring the oracle updater
section.codeblock: #... updaters: sets: - oracle config: oracle-2023-updater: url: - https://linux.oracle.com/security/oval/com.oracle.elsa-2023.xml.bz2 oracle-2022-updater: url: - https://linux.oracle.com/security/oval/com.oracle.elsa-2022.xml.bz2 #...

section.title: Configuring the photon updater
section.codeblock: #... updaters: sets: - photon config: photon: url: https://packages.vmware.com/photon/photon_oval_definitions/ #...

section.title: Configuring the rhel updater
section.codeblock: #... updaters: sets: - rhel config: rhel: url: https://access.redhat.com/security/data/oval/v2/PULP_MANIFEST ignore_unpatched: true #...
section.p: ignore_unpatched is a Boolean that indicates whether to include information about vulnerabilities that do not have corresponding patches or updates available.

section.title: Configuring the rhcc updater
section.codeblock: #... updaters: sets: - rhcc config: rhcc: url: https://access.redhat.com/security/data/metrics/cvemap.xml #...

section.title: Configuring the suse updater
section.codeblock: #... updaters: sets: - suse config: suse: url: https://support.novell.com/security/oval/ #...

section.title: Configuring the ubuntu updater
section.codeblock: #... updaters: config: ubuntu: url: https://api.launchpad.net/1.0/ name: ubuntu force: - name: focal version: 20.04 #...

dlentry.dd: Specifies the inclusion of specific distribution and version details in the resulting UpdaterSet, regardless of their status in the API response. Useful when you want to ensure that particular distributions and versions are consistently included in your updater configuration.
Specifies the distribution name that you want to force to be included in the UpdaterSet.
Specifies the version of the distribution you want to force into the UpdaterSet.

section.title: Configuring the osv updater
section.codeblock: #... updaters: sets: - osv config: osv: url: https://osv-vulnerabilities.storage.googleapis.com/ allowlist: - npm - pypi #...
section.p: allowlist is the list of ecosystems to allow. When left unset, all ecosystems are allowed. Must be lowercase.
